questions.stem: Why do large plants need transport systems but single-celled organisms do not?

options.text: Large plants have a small surface area to volume ratio, so diffusion alone is too slow
Large plants need more carbon dioxide than single-celled organisms
Single-celled organisms do not need oxygen or nutrients
Single-celled organisms have xylem and phloem inside them

questions.explanation: Large plants have a small surface area to volume ratio, meaning diffusion alone cannot supply all cells with water and nutrients quickly enough. Transport systems like xylem and phloem move substances efficiently over long distances.
